title: service_design_record.v1
description: What a service declares before it is built (00_UniversalStandards/16_Service_Design_Record.md). It defines nothing itself: it binds one service's capacity_estimate.v1, sli.v1 and slo.v1 definitions and recovery_objectives.v1 to its stores, each of which names a class from schemas/data_classes.v1.json. The Design exit gate (01_Deliverable_Lifecycle.md) requires a record that is valid against this schema and passes the relationship rules DR-001 to DR-018, whose reference behavior is tests/contracts/design_record_reference.py with vectors in schemas/examples/design_record/relationship_vectors.json.

owner.description: The GitHub user or team that owns the service.

stores.description: Every place the service keeps data, including caches and coordination records. A stateless service lists none.

mode.description: governor: an in-process bound per instance times a fixed instance count; platform_cap: the platform's concurrency limit on the trigger, for serverless consumers.

max_in_flight.description: The most requests the service holds at once across all instances.

data_class.description: The id of a class in schemas/data_classes.v1.json.

value_data.description: True when the store holds records that break a guarantee if lost or misread: money, approvals, release tokens, leases, ledgers. Such a store needs a strongly consistent class.

backup_interval_seconds.description: How often a restorable copy is taken; 0 means continuous (point-in-time recovery). Replication is not a backup: it copies a bad write too.

caches_class.description: The class of the data being cached, which sets the allowed modes and the longest TTL.
